Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and the required wake-visual inspection skill, then inspect the current rollout evidence before touching the policy. I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace and will not use or reconstruct the omitted research shelf.

The wake-visual skill applies because the sampled examples include wake keyframes. It requires anchoring the images to observations and metrics, comparing the best finite run with the most informative failure, and writing the visual diagnosis before any policy edit. I’m now inventorying all available examples and inherited logs so that comparison is evidence-based.

All four sampled rollouts are the same deterministic successful trajectory and identical keyframe sheet, despite minor source-level policy differences; there is no sampled failure sheet in this workspace. I’ll therefore use the replicated success as the visual anchor and the concrete failure/near-miss measurements retained in inherited guidance as the failure comparison, without claiming unavailable failure visuals.

The visual sheet shows a safe but slow capture: the fish first makes a large downstream/right-side lateral correction, then straightens into the developed wake and is carried upstream-left through the target at `266.255/300`. The metrics agree that mean body velocity nearly equals local flow, so the reusable mechanism is corridor acquisition and retention—not large mean thrust relative to water. The replicated run has no collision, instability, or hard-cap contact.

I found the inherited optimizer logs inside the provided `guidance_examples/` tree. They include the missing failed and near-miss rollouts, so I’m extending the required comparison to those in-workspace artifacts before writing the candidate hypothesis.

The failure comparison is now complete. The inherited `14°/0.80` policy is visibly advected downstream-right and exits after `16.75`; the `19°/0.67` policy enters the wake and remains stable but stops `5.812L` short; the `20°/0.67` policy repeats capture. I’m recording a conservative, one-mechanism interpolation hypothesis before editing the candidate, as required by the skill.

The candidate now changes one supported control axis: `20° → 20.25°` anterior amplitude, with the safety guard moved just enough to remain inactive at the new nominal scale while staying below the episode cap. I’m distilling the prior evidence—not the unevaluated candidate—into the reusable guidance bank next.

The policy, provenance notes, and reusable guidance are all updated. I’m now running the mandated non-CFD checks from `.codex/agents/check-runner.toml`: guidance materiality/provenance, Julia contract execution, and editable-boundary validation.

The first mandated check found a rendered-workspace issue: `README.md` marks the same assigned parent twice, so provenance cannot be resolved uniquely. I’ll remove only the duplicate marker (leaving the assigned parent unchanged), then rerun the check.

Guidance provenance now passes. The Julia runtime assertion cannot execute because this workspace image has no `julia` binary; I’ll still complete the remaining static schema and boundary validation so the unavailable runtime is the only check limitation.

The available checks now pass: guidance materiality/provenance, solver edit boundary, direct parameter-schema matching, and the numeric ordering `nominal acceleration < policy guard < episode cap`. I’m doing one final diff audit; no CFD rollout has been run.

The evaluator’s Julia runtime is installed at its explicit system path even though it is not on `PATH`. I found that path in the inherited evaluation logs and will rerun the exact lightweight contract assertion with it; this remains a non-CFD check.

Produced exactly one multi-wake candidate:

- [Candidate policy](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): tests `20° → 20.25°` amplitude with a `31.2 rad/time²` guard while preserving the successful steering and phasing.
- [Candidate diagnosis](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): records the visual comparison, metrics, hypothesis, and falsification boundary.
- [Reusable guidance](guidance/control_experience.md:36): adds the evidence-backed wake-corridor amplitude lesson.

All mandated non-CFD checks pass: guidance materiality, Julia policy contract, parameter schema, acceleration ordering, and solver boundary. No CFD evaluation was run.
